1.text: Sluggard. Who neglects his own and others' welfare. C. --- Disgrace. He is still despised here, and punished eternally. Matt. xxv. 30. W.

2.text: Pelted. Gr. "compared to a lump of dung." H.

3.text: Loss. "I wish," said Augustus, "I had never married, or that I had died without children." Suet.

4.text: Inheritance. Her wisdom and economy. Prov. xxxi. 29. Women had no inheritance among the Jews, when they had brothers.

5.text: Bold. In speaking and acting without restraint. C.

6.text: Mourning. S. Jer. (ep. ad Julian) quoting this sentence, calls it "divine Scripture." Prov. xxv. 20. --- Of time. Or "stripes and instruction well-timed, are wisdom." H. --- Only the wise know how to correct with advantage.

7.text: Fool. Who is incapable of understanding. Those who have sense may be corrected, though they may have taken evil courses.

9.text: This? The Athenian philosophers and Festus derided S. Paul. Acts xvii. 32.

10.text: For the fool. In the language of the Holy Ghost, he is styled a fool that turns away from God to follow vanity and sin. And what is said by the wise man against fools is meant of such fools as these. Ch. --- Their wicked life is worse than death. W.

13.text: Day. There was a longer time assigned for great men. Gen. l. 3. Num. xx. 30. and Deut. xxxiv. 8. --- Life. This is understood of those who have lost all reason, or sense of religion. S. Monica wept for her son, hoping that he would repent, as a certain bishop had comforted her. S. Aug. Conf. iii. ult.

17.text: Lead? Gold alone is heavier. But the fool is compared with lead, and is most insupportable.

19.text: Wood. Such were used in the walls of Jerusalem, (4 Mac. ii.) and of the temple and palace. 3 K. vi. 36. and vii. 12.

21.text: Cost. Of lime. C. --- Gr. omits this comparison, as well as the 23d verse. H.

23.text: Not fear. This seems contrary to what goes before. But fools are sometimes intrepid even to harshness. C.

24.text: Resentment. Or "sense," (H.) by means of pungent reprimands. C.

25.text: Away, (Gr.) Lit. "will knock them down," dejiciet. H. --- Deliberate provocations (v. 27.) are pardoned with more difficulty than a sudden impulse of wrath. v. 26. On such occasions we may withdraw our confidence, but not our charity and patience. Matt. v. 11. C. --- A true friend will not be lost for a temporal damage; but he must not be slighted. W.

29.text: Inheritance. Gr. adds, "for poverty is not always contemptible, nor is the senseless rich worthy of admiration." H.

32.text: Of him. Yet I will not follow their example. C. --- If my friend has behaved ill to me, he will be the greatest sufferer. H.

33.text: Not. Ps. cxl. 3. Who can sufficiently guard his tongue? C.
